slides.title: Self Capacitive Tactile Sensor System designed for Companion Robots
slides.tldr: SCALABLE TACTILE SENSING FOR COMPANION ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a scalable, hardware-friendly self-capacitance tactile sensing system using conductive fabric, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A scalable, FPGA-based self-capacitive tactile sensing system designed for the companion robot HIRO-chan.
card.key_idea: Uses a single conductive fabric layer and RC relaxation method, with a decision-tree classifier implemented on an FPGA to offload real-time inference from the main processor.
card.evaluation: Tested a 100-point array at 10, 100, and 1000 Hz; 100 Hz was optimal. Decision tree achieved 90.4% accuracy.
card.limitation: Limited to 100 sensors and a small set of interaction gestures, insufficient for full-body coverage.

slides.title: Assistron: Bayesian Shared Autonomy with Off-the-shelf Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: BAYESIAN SHARED AUTONOMY VIA VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work is relevant to MOSAIC as it proposes a shared autonomy model that reduces human cognitive and physical effort by combining VLA-driven macro-movements with human intervention at critical failure points.

card.one_liner: Assistron enables shared autonomy by combining frozen VLA models for macro-movements with targeted human intervention.
card.key_idea: A framework using a phase-aware interaction detector to trigger human intervention, blending joystick commands into the VLA's flow-matching process via posterior inference without fine-tuning.
card.evaluation: Tested on a multi-task scene recovery benchmark with 17 participants; showed 91.3% success rate and significantly reduced mental/physical workload versus teleoperation.
card.limitation: Bounded by the underlying VLA's semantic capabilities and assumes user corrections align with the VLA's action distribution.

slides.title: DexTeleop-0: Force-Aware Bimanual Dexterous Teleoperation with Ego-Centric Perception towards Shared Autonomy
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile-driven adaptation strategy that uses a real-time optimization loop to translate human tracking intents into force-compliant robotic commands. The approach improves success rates in contact-rich tasks by bridging the embodiment gap through tactile sensing and localized corrections.

card.one_liner: DexTeleop-0 enables precise bimanual dexterous teleoperation by combining egocentric vision with tactile-driven force optimization.
card.key_idea: A shared autonomy framework that uses a real-time QP optimization loop and operational space Jacobians to translate coarse VR tracking into force-compliant robotic commands.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in IsaacSim and on real hardware (UR7e arms, Sharpa Wave hands) across tasks like gear assembly and food sorting; showed higher success rates.

slides.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a transformer-based framework to infer binary contact states using RGB-D vision and proprioception. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and the integration of diverse sensory inputs to understand interaction states.

card.one_liner: A transformer-based framework that predicts binary fingertip contact using only RGB-D vision and robot proprioception.
card.key_idea: Fuses RGB-D tokens with current and commanded joint configurations via cross-attention, using a causal transformer to capture temporal dynamics for pseudo-tactile contact estimation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via F1 scores and in-hand reorientation tasks (CRR/CRA) on seen/novel objects in simulation and on a real LEAP hand.
card.limitation: Performance degrades on real hardware, particularly for non-convex geometries where rapid contact events are heavily occluded.

slides.title: BiliVLA: Scene-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Biliary Endoscopic Navigation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Vision-Language-Action framework using reinforcement learning for autonomous endoscopic navigation, contributing to MIMIC's interest in LLM-based agent models for complex task execution.

card.one_liner: BiliVLA enables autonomous biliary endoscopic navigation using a scene-aware Vision-Language-Action framework with reinforcement learning.
card.key_idea: A two-stage training paradigm combining grounding-enhanced supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to predict target categories, bounding boxes, and 3-DoF motor commands.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three ERCP subtasks using a phantom model; achieved 91.96% action precision and 84.85% success rate, outperforming EndoVLA and Qwen3-VL.
card.limitation: Evaluations were conducted in phantom environments; future work is needed for ex vivo tissue and diverse visual degradations.

slides.title: LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces a safety benchmark and dataset for Vision-Language-Action models, addressing the tension between generalization and safety in embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: LIBERO-Safety is a comprehensive benchmark evaluating physical and semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
card.key_idea: A parametric benchmark using UBDDL for procedural scene generation and a keypose-driven pipeline to synthesize 19,664 collision-free demonstrations via an optimization-based motion planner.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 8 VLA and 2 foundation models across 75 tasks using Success Rate, Collision Rate, and Refusal Rate; results show critical OOD vulnerabilities.
card.limitation: Task success is bottlenecked by sub-optimal trajectory synthesis and semantic misalignment, even when physical safety constraints are maintained.

slides.title: WOLF-VLA: Whole-Body Humanoid Optimal Locomotion Framework for Vision-Language-Action Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces WOLF-VLA, a framework that enables humanoid robots to generate whole-body locomotion policies from natural-language instructions. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework using optimal-control trajectories to train VLAs for dynamically consistent whole-body humanoid locomotion.
card.key_idea: Integrates an OC-based motion synthesis pipeline to generate a large-scale, physically optimal dataset of humanoid trajectories for training a transformer-based VLA model.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six locomotion tasks using success rates and ROM error; outperformed ACT and pi 0.5 baselines in MuJoCo simulation.
card.limitation: Evaluations were conducted exclusively in a virtual simulation environment using the RH5 humanoid model.

slides.title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: PRETRAINING ACTION PRIORS FOR CROSS-EMBODIMENT VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: A two-stage training framework introduces a flow-matching-based action module to learn temporal motion structure before VLA alignment, improving convergence and success rates in data-scarce tasks.

card.one_liner: A two-stage framework that pretrains an action module on motion priors to accelerate VLA convergence.
card.key_idea: A flow-matching encoder-decoder learns temporal motion from action trajectories (Stage 1), then transfers this prior to VLA training via decoder reuse, latent distillation, and history compression (Stage 2).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 13 cross-embodiment tasks (LIBERO, RoboCasa, real-world Franka). Results show higher success rates and faster convergence compared to from-scratch VLA training and baselines.
